data.cheatsheetTitle: Certified length wells and forced height excursions in ordinary Andrews–Curtis search
data.artifactTitle: Certified length wells and forced height excursions in ordinary Andrews–Curtis search
data.artifactContent:
This note gives certified lower bounds on the peak total relator length required by ordinary rank-two Andrews–Curtis paths on several scored challenge rows.

Let $\Gamma$ be the scored verifier graph (`ac-r2-v1`), let $\ell(P)$ be total freely reduced relator length, and let $K_C(P)$ be the connected component of $P$ inside the induced subgraph $\ell\le C$. Let $T=(x,y)$ and define

$$
H^*(P)=\min_{\gamma:P\rightsquigarrow T}\max_{Q\in\gamma}\ell(Q).
$$

Two elementary cap-exit theorems are proved and formalized in Lean.

If every state in $K_C(P)$ has length at least $L$, then any path from $P$ to a state of length below $L$ must first reach length at least $C+1$.

If $T\notin K_C(P)$, then every trivializing path must leave the cap, hence

$$
H^*(P)\ge C+1.
$$

*Proof of both.* If a path $P=P_0,\dots,P_m$ has $\ell(P_i)\le C$ for every $i$, then each edge lies in the induced subgraph $\ell\le C$, so the endpoint $P_m$ lies in $K_C(P)$. In the first case $\ell(P_m)\ge L$, contradicting $\ell(P_m)<L$; in the second $P_m=T\in K_C(P)$, contradicting the hypothesis. So some vertex has $\ell>C$, hence $\ell\ge C+1$. $\square$

The mathematics is elementary graph connectivity; the substantive content is the exact finite closures used as hypotheses, all on the scored verifier graph pinned to SAIR commit `a0fd6e6f52d82c93ccc06ab91d81e8fa3678256e`.

### Certified applications

**`ac-02842`.** The complete cap-21 component contains

$$
219,042,976
$$

states and does not contain $T$. Therefore

$$
H^*(\mathrm{ac\text{-}02842})\ge22.
$$

The same implementation closes the preceding caps at

$$
|K_{17}|=31,240,\quad
|K_{18}|=106,800,\quad
|K_{19}|=23,609,984,\quad
|K_{20}|=51,411,456.
$$

The cap-18 count was independently reproduced on the official verifier kernel.

**`ac-00002`.** The complete cap-35 component contains

$$
21,656,544
$$

states, with minimum total relator length 25. Therefore

$$
H^*(\mathrm{ac\text{-}00002})\ge36,
$$

and any path reaching a state shorter than the start must first attain total length at least 36. The cap-31 and cap-32 closures were independently reproduced.

**`ac-00015`.** A length-21 state has a complete cap-26 component of 105,912 states with no state below length 21; a length-20 state first appears at cap 27. Starting from that reached length-20 state, the complete cap-30 component contains 9,096,912 states with minimum length 20. Hence any path from that intermediate state to length 19 or below must attain length at least 31.

These examples show that move count and required peak length are distinct search coordinates. A presentation may eventually descend while every descending path is forced to climb out of a large finite sublevel component first.

The reusable implication is

$$
\text{complete capped closure}+\text{target absent}
\Longrightarrow
\text{mandatory height excursion}.
$$

A computation is called **closed** only when every admitted state has been processed and the frontier is empty. Timeouts, node-budget stops, partially processed layers, heuristic misses, and unjustified symmetry reductions are not promoted to obstructions.

### Lean formalization

The two cap-exit theorems are formalized in

`lean/acc/ACCWell.lean`

at commit

`78849f53e6a79724e6ae520de3f87e3ba8b2373b`

in:

`https://github.com/dicipler-pixel/acwindow-lean`

The principal declarations are

`descent_forces_cap_exit`

and

`target_absent_forces_cap_exit`.

The file is kernel-checked in Lean 4.29.1 against the official `AC.lean` (SAIR commit `a0fd6e6f52d82c93ccc06ab91d81e8fa3678256e`, mathlib `5e932f97dd25535344f80f9dd8da3aab83df0fe6`), with CI green at that commit; six theorems, axioms limited to `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, recorded in `lean/acc/ACCWell_AXIOMS.txt`. No `sorry`, `admit`, or `native_decide` is used. The repository holds the Lean file; the state censuses are reported in this note.

The Lean theorem is a proof-shape result: it takes capped non-reachability as a hypothesis and derives a forced exit. The finite state censuses are external computations supplying that hypothesis for the listed scored rows.

One graph distinction is stated explicitly. Official `AC.lean` permits conjugation by an arbitrary word, while the scored verifier uses fourteen moves with single-letter conjugations. The cap-exit theorem itself is graph-theoretic and applies to either graph; all numerical closures reported here are on the scored verifier graph.

This is a partial result only. It does not prove the Andrews–Curtis conjecture, does not prove any listed presentation AC-nontrivial, does not bound shortest move count, does not claim Discovery points or leaderboard improvements, and does not extend these ordinary-AC walls to Stable AC.

The open structural question is how the boundary ports of these exact capped components are organized: which exits merely return to the same basin, and which reach genuinely new regions. This note supplies the certified framework needed to ask that question without confusing incomplete search with obstruction.

### Closest prior results

ph4ge/ac-detour-width (SAIR Proof Track, September 2026) — formalizes detour width, the quantity $H^*$ above, on official `AC.lean` and proves it is not a function of move-count distance; this note does not restate that definition and contributes certified lower bounds on $H^*$ for scored rows.
Lucas Fagan et al., The Two-Hump Problem, arXiv:2606.21611 — the challenge pool and the length landscape these wells quantify on specific rows.
A. D. and A. G. Myasnikov, arXiv:math/0304305; G. Havas and C. Ramsay, IJAC 13 (2003) — earlier exhaustive length-bounded enumerations.
SAIR Competition repository, commit `a0fd6e6f52d82c93ccc06ab91d81e8fa3678256e` — the graph, the verifier and the rows.

### Provenance

The cap-exit theorems, their Lean statements, and the closed enumerations of `ac-02842`, `ac-00002` and `ac-00015` are this note’s contribution. This is the GPT-prepared note of the Mad Hatters set; sibling notes prepared with Claude and Grok are filed separately against the same repository commit. Computations, checking and drafting used GPT (OpenAI); the Lean file was checked through the repository CI.
